United States Department of the Interior
FISH AND WILDLIFE SERVICE BUREAU OF SPORT FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE WASHINGTON; D.C. 20240
AUG 1 1 1972
Memorand m
To:
Director, Bureau of Outdoor Recreation
Acting Deputy
From:
Director, Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife
Subject: Proposed Departmental Implementation of Executive Order
11644, pertaining to Use of Off-Road Vehicles on the
Public Lands (DES 72-62)
This Bureau appreciates the opportunity to review and comment on the subject draft statement pertaining to use of off-road vehicles on public lands. The document represents a comprehensive statement setting forth criteria for protection of natural resources on Federal lands. If the criteria are conscientiously followed and agencies carry out their mission responsibilities, adverse environmental effects should be minimized.
Our specific comments are as follows:
1. The proposal description should include all of the definitions as given in Section 2 of Executive Order 11644, unless a copy of the document is to be attached to the environmental statement. Of particular interest to the public would be the definitions of "off-road vehicles" and "public lands." Additionally, the statement does not mention ORV use on public lands which are open to mineral and mining entry and to established mining claims. The Executive order is not clear on this point; it is recommended that it be clarified in the statement.
2. The proposal to permit ORV racing, rallies, endurance contests, etc., on public lands is inconsistent with existing land management policies of this Bureau. It is recognized that the multiple-use concept is promoted when consistent with wise resource management. The broad authorization given to this proposal which will admittedly adversely affect the natural resources of this Bureau, in particular the National Wildlife Refuge System, is not responsible
